rites.name: Ilomaum
rites.text: Ilomaum is the concept of a resonant root-tone that rang through the first groves of Vhoggaktak during the Singing, binding loose earth into the first kingdoms. It is less a thing than a pattern that growing realms learned to imitate and call upon.

rites.name: Osezith
rites.text: Osezith is the concept of the Seeding in Vhoggaktak, the moment when the makers press the Weave into the soil of the Martial Realm and the sleeping powers are stilled beneath it. It is not a being but an idea held in the Third Era's record, a pause where strength is set aside before it wakes.

rites.name: Eliolanae
rites.text: Eliolanae is the concept of the Weave, the thread-lattice the makers plant during the Seeding so that quiet powers may sleep within the world. In the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders, it is the principle by which hearths are kindled and oaths are bound to the sky.

rites.name: Thazhak
rites.text: Thazhak is a concept of the Weave in the Seeding, the quiet pattern the makers plant to hold powers in sleep during the Holy Age of flame and temple orders. It is never a body or a place, only the idea that a force can be bound and waked again. Its record lies in the stories of the orders that first learned to kindle and dampen it.

rites.name: Druzhourkak
rites.text: Druzhourkak is a seventy-two segment sacred cipher forged in the Martial realm during the sixth era, its three-letter fragments each binding a warding spirit of the first order. Wardens of the Vhoggaktak wastes carve its segments into iron to still charging beasts and to shield frontier keeps from collapsing walls.

rites.name: Alaanneilae
rites.text: Alaanneilae is a concept in Vhoggaktak, born when the Three Futures split and the Library began shelving every possible ending. It is held in the Martial Realm as a doctrine of flame and discipline, its teachings carried by temple orders through the Holy Age.
